reflection.zh: 这项免费牙科护理的承诺，体现了政府“施行公义和正直”的呼召，以确保公民的基本福祉。雅伟的话语提醒执政者，他们的职责是关怀弱势群体，为共同利益服务，使基本服务惠及所有人。

title.en: Search for survivors after 16 killed by Russian double-tap strike on Ukraine mall
title.zh: 官员称，俄罗斯无人机“双重打击”致乌克兰购物中心15人死亡

summary.en: Officials reported that a Russian drone strike on a shopping center in Ukraine killed 15 people and injured 130 others, including 23 children.
summary.zh: 官员报告称，俄罗斯对乌克兰一购物中心的无人机袭击造成15人死亡，另有130人受伤，其中包括23名儿童。

body.en:
Rescuers in Ukraine worked through the night to search for survivors in the wreckage of a shopping centre hit by a deadly Russian double-tap drone strike.

Sixteen people were killed and 130 injured in the busy mall in Kryvyi Rih on Friday, local officials said. Nine people are reportedly still missing.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said the "cynical and despicable" attack was carried out in two waves, with the second strike targeting emergency workers at the scene.

Meanwhile, local officials said at least two people had been killed by further Russian strikes early on Saturday. The defence ministry in Moscow said it had targeted transport infrastructure and warehouses.

Twenty-three children are among those injured by Friday's attack on the shopping centre in the Dnipropetrovsk region, said regional military head Oleksandr Hanzha.

Hanzha said the death toll had reached 16 after another body was retrieved from the rubble overnight. He previously said 29 people were in a serious condition, prompting fears the toll could rise further.

Dramatic footage verified by the BBC showed the second drone hitting the already burning mall in Zelensky's hometown. Russia's military has not commented.

Rescue teams from four other Ukrainian regions were urgently deployed to help search for survivors.

Kryvyi Rih Mayor Oleksandr Vilkul said the Russian drones were flying at "extremely low altitudes", describing the attackers as "animals".

As rescue efforts continued overnight, local authorities in Kyiv said one person had been killed after a fire broke out in a warehouse following an alert for a ballistic missile.

In the southern city of Zaporizhzhia, a Russian drone strike killed at least one man and injured four people, according to Ivan Fedorov, the head of the regional military administration.

Four people - including three children - were killed in separate Russian attacks in Ukraine's southern Mykolaiv region on Friday, and another two in the north-eastern Kharkiv region, local officials said.

And on Thursday 17 people were killed and more than 40 injured in a major Russian missile and drone attack on Ukraine's capital Kyiv .

Earlier on Friday, Ukraine's military said it carried out strikes on an oil refinery and a military airfield deep inside Russia.

Ukraine has in recent months intensified attacks on Russian energy facilities, as well as on warehouses of the country's largest online retailer Wildberries.

Kyiv describes them as legitimate targets because they help finance Russia's war.

Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and currently Moscow controls about a fifth of Ukrainian territory in the south-east.
body.zh: 当地官员称，俄罗斯无人机对乌克兰中部城市克里沃罗格的一家购物中心发动两次无人机袭击，造成至少 15 人死亡。 该市最大的购物中心另有 130 人受伤，其中包括 23 名儿童。据报道还有更多人被困在废墟中。 泽伦斯基总统表示，他的家乡白天发生的袭击“绝对是愤世嫉俗和卑鄙的”，分“两波”进行，第二次袭击针对的是现场的急救人员。 英国广播公司证实的戏剧性镜头显示，第二架无人机袭击了第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克地区已经燃烧的购物中心。俄罗斯军方尚未发表评论。 第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克地区负责人亚历山大·汉扎 (Oleksandr Hanzha) 周五晚间表示，目前已确认有 15 人死亡，其中两人后来在医院死亡。 他说，共有130人受伤，其中29人伤势严重。人们担心死亡人数会进一步上升。 来自乌克兰其他四个地区的救援队正在紧急部署，以帮助寻找幸存者。 当天早些时候，克里沃罗格市市长亚历山大·维尔库尔表示，俄罗斯无人机在“极低的高度”飞行，并将袭击者描述为“动物”。 此前一天，俄罗斯导弹和无人机对乌克兰首都基辅发动大规模袭击，造成 17 人死亡、40 多人受伤。 当地官员称，全市多处公寓楼和仓库一夜之间遭到袭击。儿童医院和学校也遭到破坏。 周五早些时候，乌克兰军方表示，他们对俄罗斯境内的一座炼油厂和一座军用机场进行了袭击。 近几个月来，乌克兰加大了对俄罗斯能源设施以及该国最大在线零售商 Wildberry 仓库的攻击力度。 基辅将它们描述为合法目标，因为它们为俄罗斯的战争提供资金。 俄罗斯总统普京于2022年2月对乌克兰发动全面入侵，目前莫斯科控制着乌克兰东南部约五分之一的领土。

reflection.en: The tragic loss of life and widespread injuries in this attack bring immense sorrow and pain, especially with children among the victims. In moments of such profound grief, we hold onto the promise that one day, Yahweh will wipe away every tear, and death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more. This hope anchors us, even as we lament the present...
reflection.zh: 这次袭击中生命的悲惨逝去和广泛的伤亡带来了巨大的悲伤和痛苦，尤其是有儿童受害。在如此深重的悲痛时刻，我们紧紧抓住雅伟的应许，有一天他将擦去所有的眼泪，死亡、悲哀、哭号和疼痛都将不再有。这份盼望成为我们的锚，即使我们为当前的苦难哀叹。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: Canada vows to match Trump’s 50% tariffs after trade deal talks fail
title.zh: 加拿大誓言在贸易谈判失败后对特朗普的50%关税进行对等报复

summary.en: Trade negotiations between the United States and Canada have collapsed, with Canada vowing to retaliate with matching tariffs after accusing Washington of last-minute changes to the proposed deal.
summary.zh: 美国和加拿大之间的贸易谈判破裂，加拿大指责华盛顿在拟议协议中临时修改条款，并誓言将以对等关税进行报复。

body.en: Mark Carney accuses Washington of ‘unfair’ last-minute changes to deal, as US and Canada fail to reach agreement after three-day extension of talks Canadian prime minister Mark Carney has promised to match US tariffs “dollar for dollar”, after the two sides failed to agree a trade deal by the deadline of midnight on Friday. Canadian officials had worked hard in good faith but “last-minute changes in the US proposed terms were unfair, uneconomic and called into question the reliability of any deal”, Carney said in a statement. Continue reading...

While complete agreement isn't always possible, this verse reminds us of the call to pursue peace as much as it depends on us, even when faced with perceived unfairness. It encourages a posture of seeking harmony, even when...

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Battery fires at recycling centres are costing UK £1bn a year, figures show
title.zh: 电池火灾每年给英国回收中心造成10亿英镑损失

summary.en: Figures show that fires caused by wrongly discarded lithium batteries, such as those found in vapes, are costing UK recycling centers £1 billion a year and putting lives at risk. Experts report more than 10 such fires occur weekly.
summary.zh: 数据显示，由错误丢弃的锂电池（例如电子烟中的电池）引起的火灾，每年给英国回收中心造成10亿英镑的损失，并危及生命。专家报告称，每周发生超过10起此类火灾。

body.en: Experts say fires caused by wrongly discarded lithium batteries, such as those in vapes, are putting lives at risk Fires at recycling centres caused by wrongly discarded lithium batteries such as those found in vapes are occurring at the rate of more than 10 a week, according to new figures. Experts say the sheer volume of battery fires now occurring at waste facilities has reached a crisis that is putting lives at risk, costing £1bn a year and frustrating fire chiefs. Continue reading...

Proverbs 27:12 reminds us that the prudent anticipate danger and take necessary precautions, while a lack of care can lead to costly and dangerous consequences. This calls us to consider the full lifecycle...

title.en: ‘We fear lessons will not be learned’: Chloe Moffat’s parents on their fight to hold Treasury to account
title.zh: “我们担心教训不会被吸取”：克洛伊·莫法特的父母为追究财政部责任而战

summary.en: The parents of Chloe Moffat are considering legal action for wrongful death after a coroner concluded that a disciplinary process at the Treasury materially contributed to her suicide. They are fighting to ensure that lessons are learned from their daughter's death.
summary.zh: 在一名验尸官裁定财政部的一个纪律程序“实质性地促成了”克洛伊·莫法特（Chloe Moffat）的自杀后，她的父母正在考虑就非正常死亡提起诉讼。他们正在努力确保从女儿的死亡中吸取教训。

body.en: Couple considering suing for wrongful death after coroner found disciplinary process materially contributed to suicide When a coroner ruled this month that the Treasury “materially contributed” to Chloe Moffat’s death , her parents breathed out in bittersweet relief. For a year, David and Anne Moffat had been forced to become detectives in the worst case any parent could have to solve: why their daughter took her own life. Chloe, 26, went to her job as a personal assistant at the Treasury on a Monday last May “happy as Larry” after a weekend she’d told her friends was a “10 out of 10”. She was planning a holiday with her sister, Alice, and arranging for friends to come for a dinner party the next weekend. She was, according to her father, living “the best life”. Continue reading...
body.zh: 验尸官发现纪律程序对自杀造成重大影响后，一对夫妇考虑以非正常死亡为由提起诉讼 当验尸官本月裁定财政部对克洛伊·莫法特的死亡“有重大贡献”时，她的父母苦乐参半地松了口气。一年来，大卫和安妮·莫法特被迫成为侦探，应对任何父母都必须解决的最糟糕的情况：他们的女儿为什么自杀。去年 5 月的一个星期一，26 岁的克洛伊 (Chloe) 去财政部担任私人助理，她告诉朋友们，在经历了一个“十分之十”的周末后，她“像拉里一样快乐”。她正计划与姐姐爱丽丝一起度假，并安排朋友下周末来参加晚宴。据她父亲说，她过着“最好的生活”。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The profound despair described in this verse echoes the tragic circumstances of Chloe Moffat's death, where an institutional process contributed to her overwhelming suffering. Her parents' courageous fight for accountability reminds us that systems must be designed with compassion and care, preventing individuals from reaching such a breaking point. It...
reflection.zh: 这节经文所描述的深切绝望，与克洛伊·莫法特（Chloe Moffat）的悲剧性死亡情况相呼应，其中一个制度流程导致了她极度的痛苦。她父母为问责而进行的勇敢抗争提醒我们，制度必须以同情和关怀来设计，防止个人达到崩溃的边缘。它呼吁我们反思我们的结构如何能更好地支持人类福祉，并防止如此巨大的损失。

verse.textEn: He came to a broom bush, sat down under it and prayed that he might die. 'I have had enough, Yahweh,' he said. 'Take my life; I am no better than my ancestors.'
verse.textZh: 他自己在旷野走了一日的路程，来到一棵罗腾树下，就坐在那里求死，说：「雅伟啊，罢了！求你取我的性命，因为我不胜于我的列祖。」

title.en: Canada says it will match US tariffs 'dollar for dollar' as trade talks break down
title.zh: 加拿大称将“一美元对一美元”对等征收美国关税，贸易谈判破裂

summary.en: After trade talks collapsed, the US imposed a new 50% levy on $20 billion of Canadian imports. Canada announced it would respond by matching these tariffs "dollar for dollar."
summary.zh: 贸易谈判破裂后，美国对价值200亿美元的加拿大进口商品征收50%的新关税。加拿大宣布将“一美元对一美元”地对等征收关税以作回应。

body.en:
A fresh wave of US tariffs on a wide array of Canadian goods came into effect on Saturday after a last-minute breakdown in trade talks.

Announcing the suspension of negotiations shortly before the Friday night deadline, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he would impose reciprocal tariffs on US goods "dollar for dollar".

Carney said "last-minute changes in the US proposed terms were unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal".

Trade negotiators had been engaged in intense talks since July, after President Donald Trump threatened to impose a 50% levy on nearly $20bn (C$28bn) of Canadian imports by 19 August.

Trump had temporarily paused those tariffs earlier in the week, saying the two sides were close to signing a trade deal that was "very good" for both countries.

But minutes before the deadline for a deal, Carney said that while "important progress" had been made in the talks it was "not enough to meet our objectives for Canadians".

"As a result, this evening, I have decided to suspend trade negotiations with the US and have directed negotiators to return to Ottawa," he said.

"Last-minute changes in the US proposed terms were unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal."

After Carney's announcement US trade representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement: "Tonight, Canada declined to finalise the trade deal under the terms agreed earlier this week.

"Despite the US offer to Canada to receive the best treatment of any major exporter to our market, new demands and walk backs of other commitments by Canada have upended the careful balance reached in the past days."

The breakdown in talks marks a significant shift in tone from earlier in the week, when both US and Canadian officials sounded optimistic that a trade deal beneficial for both countries was within reach.

Negotiators were reportedly discussing a deal that would reduce US tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminium from 50% to 25%, and on Canadian autos from 25% to 15%.

In exchange, Carney had asked Canadian provinces to restore US alcohol to store shelves.

Tensions between the two major trading partners have been simmering since Trump returned to office in January last year and unleashed a wide-ranging global programme of tariffs, upending decades of free trade between Canada and the US.

Now that talks have broken down, Canada will be hit with new 50% US tariffs imposed by Trump using a Depression-era law called the Tariff Act of 1930.

They will be applied on a range of goods, including wine, dairy, cement, clothing and hockey equipment.

They are in addition to existing tariffs the US had already imposed on Canadian steel and aluminium, autos and lumber.

body.zh: 在贸易谈判最后一刻破裂后，美国对多种加拿大商品征收的新一波关税于周六生效。 加拿大总理马克·卡尼在周五晚上最后期限前不久宣布暂停谈判，表示他将对美国商品“一美元对一美元”征收互惠关税。 卡尼表示，“美国提议的条款在最后一刻发生的变化是不公平的、不经济的，并且使任何协议的可靠性受到质疑”。 在唐纳德·特朗普总统威胁要在 8 月 19 日之前对近 200 亿美元（280 亿加元）的加拿大进口商品征收 50% 的关税后，自 7 月以来，贸易谈判代表一直在进行激烈的谈判。 特朗普本周早些时候暂时暂停了这些关税，称双方即将签署一项对两国“非常好”的贸易协议。 但在达成协议的最后期限前几分钟，卡尼表示，虽然谈判取得了“重要进展”，但“还不足以实现我们为加拿大人制定的目标”。 “因此，今晚，我决定暂停与美国的贸易谈判，并指示谈判代表返回渥太华，”他说。 “美国提议的条款在最后一刻发生变化是不公平的、不经济的，并且使任何协议的可靠性受到质疑。” 卡尼宣布这一消息后，美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔在一份声明中表示：“今晚，加拿大拒绝根据本周早些时候商定的条款敲定贸易协议。 “尽管美国向加拿大提出要获得我们市场上所有主要出口国的最佳待遇，但新的要求以及加拿大对其他承诺的反悔，已经颠覆了过去几天达成的谨慎平衡。” 谈判的破裂标志着与本周早些时候相比基调的重大转变，当时美国和加拿大官员都对达成对两国有利的贸易协议表示乐观。 据报道，谈判代表正在讨论一项协议，将美国对加拿大钢铁和铝的关税从 50% 降低到 25%，对加拿大汽车的关税从 25% 降低到 15%。 作为交换，卡尼要求加拿大各省将美国酒恢复到商店货架上。 自特朗普去年1月重返办公室并推出广泛的全球关税计划以来，这两个主要贸易伙伴之间的紧张关系一直在酝酿，颠覆了加拿大和美国之间数十年的自由贸易。 现在谈判破裂，加拿大将受到特朗普根据大萧条时期的《1930 年关税法》征收的 50% 新关税的打击。 它们将应用于一系列商品，包括葡萄酒、乳制品、水泥、服装和曲棍球设备。 这是美国对加拿大钢铁、铝、汽车和木材征收的现有关税的补充。 道格·福特 (Doug Ford) 是一向直言不讳的加拿大总理……

title.en: Lindsay Clancy suffering 'command hallucination' when she killed children, court hears
title.zh: 法庭获悉，林赛·克兰西在杀害孩子时遭受“指令性幻觉”

summary.en: The defense presented its final witness, a forensic psychiatrist, who testified about the severe effects of postpartum psychosis in the case of Lindsay Clancy.
summary.zh: 辩方传唤了最后一名证人——一名法医精神病学家出庭作证，阐述了产后精神病对林赛·克兰西案件的严重影响。

body.en:
Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mum who has been charged with murdering her three children, was suffering from a "command hallucination" at the time, a forensic psychiatrist has told the jury in her trial.

The defence, which rested its case on Friday, does not dispute that Clancy carried out the killings but say she has pleaded not guilty to murder charges because she was experiencing postpartum psychosis.

Forensic psychiatrist Phillip Resnick, the defence's final witness, testified about the effects of postpartum psychosis.

Prosecutors, meanwhile, alleged she made a calculated decision to intentionally kill her children - Cora, five, Dawson, three, and Callan, who was eight months.

"My opinion is that Ms Clancy was, due to her mental disease, unable to conform her conduct to the requirements of the law on the day that she took the lives of her children," Resnick told jurors. "It was a matter where she was just following the command rather than being able to make any decision to do it or not."

The forensic psychiatrist said that in his opinion on the day Clancy killed her children she experienced "not only a command hallucination" but also "a delusion of influence".

Clancy lacked control and was likely unable to tell the difference between right and wrong on that January 2023 day, he told the jury on Friday.

"In her mind, she believed that she would be doing her children a favour by having them go to heaven with her rather than remain on earth without her doing the mothering," Resnick testified.

The case is expected to go to the jury early next week following nearly a month of witness testimony.

Earlier this week, Clancy's mother and former mother-in-law testified about how Clancy's mental health deteriorated after the birth of her youngest son.

"She was begging for help," Clancy's former mother-in-law, Susan Clancy, said of a woman she described as a "very nurturing, very loving" mother.

Prosecutors have said that in January 2023, Clancy intentionally strangled the three children with fitness bands in their Massachusetts home before jumping out of a second-floor window. Clancy, now 36, was paralysed by the jump and has attended the trial in a wheelchair.

The defence have said Clancy experienced hallucinations and delusions after giving birth to Callan and she was undergoing medical treatment for psychiatric problems. She checked herself into a psychiatric hospital for a few days just before the deaths.

The UK's National Health Service (NHS) defines postpartum psychosis as a rare serious mental health illness that can affect someone soon after having a baby.

"Postpartum psychosis is very different from the 'baby blues'," the NHS adds. "It's a serious mental illness and should be treated as a medical emergency."

title.en: Russian drones hit Ukraine mall, killing 16 and wounding 13 including children
title.zh: 俄罗斯无人机袭击乌克兰购物中心，造成16人死亡，包括儿童在内的13人受伤

summary.en: Russian drones struck a mall in Ukraine, resulting in 16 deaths and 13 injuries, including children. This attack marks an escalation in Russia's air war as the conflict approaches its four-and-a-half-year mark.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯无人机袭击了乌克兰一家购物中心，造成16人死亡，包括儿童在内的13人受伤。此次袭击标志着俄罗斯空战的升级，两国冲突已持续近四年半。

body.en:
At least 16 people have been killed and more than 130 wounded ‌when Russian drones struck an Ukraine shopping centre, an attack President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as an "act of barbarism".

Regional ‌governor Oleksandr Hanzha said that 22 children were among the wounded in the daytime attack on the city of Kryvyi Rih, which is Zelenskyy's hometown.

"There are 29 people in serious condition, including five children," Hanzha said. He posted a photo of ‌black smoke billowing ‌from a ⁠large industrial building.

In an update early on Saturday, Hanzha said nine people were preliminarily considered missing, including two children, and that rescuers were continuing to clear the rubble of the shopping centre.

Zelenskyy called the attack "absolutely cynical and despicable", saying that a second Russian drone hit the shopping centre half an hour after the first ⁠in what he said was a deliberate ‌attempt to target emergency services.

"Attacks like these are nothing less than terrorist acts," Zelenskky said on Telegram, urging ‌the world to hold Russia to account. "We will definitely respond."

In a separate attack on Friday, at least four people, including three children, were killed and a woman was wounded after a Russian drone strike in Ukraine's southern region of Mykolaiv, Ukrainian state media said on Telegram.

Russia is escalating its air ‌war on Ukraine as fighting on the battlefield grinds toward the 4-1/2-year mark. On Thursday, 17 people were killed in a Russian ballistic missile attack on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv.

Ukraine has also stepped up its own attacks on Russia, targeting oil facilities and logistics infrastructure to try to undermine Moscow's ability to wage war.

title.en: 'Quiet, quiet, quiet!' - What triggers Trump to shut down reporters?
title.zh: “安静，安静，安静！”——是什么触发了特朗普让记者闭嘴？

summary.en: A BBC report examines the types of questions that lead the US president to insult journalists and abruptly end interviews.
summary.zh: 英国广播公司的一篇报道审视了那些导致美国总统侮辱记者并突然结束采访的问题类型。

body.en:
President Donald Trump has been lashing out at reporters, often female journalists, when confronted with questions he does not like to answer.

The BBC's Tom Bateman takes a look at what triggers these public insults, and what are the questions the president doesn’t want to be asked.

reflection.en: The power of words is immense, capable of both piercing and healing. This report highlights how public figures' responses to scrutiny can shape the tone of public discourse. Yahweh calls us to use our speech wisely, seeking to build up rather than tear down, even when facing difficult questions.
reflection.zh: 言语的力量是巨大的，既能刺伤人，也能带来医治。这篇报道突显了公众人物面对审视时的回应方式，如何塑造公共话语的基调。雅伟呼召我们智慧地运用言语，即使面对难题，也要寻求造就而非拆毁。

title.en: Myanmar military strike kills 14 attending monastery retreat
title.zh: 缅甸军事打击致14名参加寺院静修者死亡

summary.en: The Myanmar military conducted an airstrike on a monastery retreat, killing 14 civilians. This incident follows a UN report indicating the military's increased use of low-cost aircraft for civilian casualties.
summary.zh: 缅甸军方对一处寺院静修地发动空袭，造成14名平民死亡。此前联合国一份报告指出，缅甸军方越来越多地使用低成本飞机杀害平民。

body.en:
An air strike by Myanmar's military on a Buddhist monastery in the central Sagaing region has killed 14 people who were taking part in a week-long meditation retreat, an opposition group and a resident say.

The attack is the latest in a series of frequent and deadly aerial strikes targeting armed anti-government forces and ethnic armed groups in the country.

Two weeks ago, an United Nations report said Myanmar’s military has increasingly used low-cost aircraft such as motorized paragliders and gyrocopters in escalating aerial attacks that kill civilians in its conflict with armed, anti-government groups.

The report by the UN-established Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar, or IIMM, details a yearlong investigation into alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity committed by Myanmar’s military and affiliated militias, as well as the opposition armed groups.

Myanmar’s military government did not immediately respond to either the UN probe. In the past, the military has said it only attacks legitimate targets of war, accusing the resistance forces of being terrorists.

The monastery attack occurred on Friday in Swel Le Oh village in Myaung township, about 75km west of Mandalay, the country's second largest city, according to Nway Oo, a spokesman for the Civil Defence and Security Organisation of Myaung Township, or CDSOM.

Nway Oo said 14 people, including three women, were killed and 20 others were wounded when a jet fighter dropped a bomb in the compound of the village's monastery.

A villager who spoke on condition of anonymity also confirmed the death toll to the Associated Press.

The villager said the jet fighter dropped two bombs 15 minutes apart, with the second bomb damaging a house near the monastery where more than 100 people were on a week-long retreat.

The villager, whose mother-in-law was killed in the air strike, said that people fled to a nearby community after cremating bodies of the victims.

The BBC's Burmese-language service and Myanmar's media outlets, including Myanmar Now, reported the death toll at between 10 and 14.

They also posted photos and videos showing what they said was the aftermath of the strike, with images of bodies.

title.en: As they return to the UK, Harry and Meghan search for a brand that sticks
title.zh: 哈里和梅根回英国后，寻找一个能立足的品牌

summary.en: Harry and Meghan are returning to the UK but will no longer be working royals. The news speculates on what new roles or ventures they might pursue instead.

body.en:
In late July, the Duchess of Sussex's lifestyle range, called As ever, launched a "rich, vibrant" blackberry spread alongside a softly lit video of her picking the fruit.

A month later, Meghan and her husband Prince Harry are returning to live in the UK just as blackberry season ends. Perhaps we can expect another video soon, shot on these shores.

Or perhaps not, because experts say the Harry and Meghan brand is at a crossroads.

After the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's acrimonious exit from the Royal Family in 2020, the projects marking their fresh start in California - from streaming to signature scents - have mostly failed to find large audiences, and experts say it's unclear where the couple goes from here.

Their return to the UK has surprised many and we don't know their reasons for the switch, but what's clear is that they will not be working royals when they return. So what could they be doing instead?

Andrew Stephen, the L'Oréal professor of marketing at the University of Oxford's Saïd Business School, says that after they moved to the US the Sussexes "attracted enormous attention and were initially very good at monetising it. But I don't think they have been as successful at converting that initial success into an enduring brand."

Now, he says, they have a "fragmented portfolio spanning social impact, entertainment and lifestyle, which has made it difficult to know exactly what their brand stands for".

After splitting with the Royal Family, the Sussexes said they would work to become financially independent. They began life as civilians with interviews about their relationship with the royals before pivoting to new fields of interest, including media production and lifestyle, which now appears to be Meghan's focus.

The couple's aim, according to the mission statement of their Archewell Productions company, is to highlight "our common humanity and celebrate community". They have continued to promote the Invictus Games, the sporting event for injured service men and women that Prince Harry founded, and launched charitable projects around the world through Archewell Philanthropies.

They are widely reported to have earned $100m (£73m) from a deal with Netflix in 2020. An agreement in the same year with Spotify to produce podcasts was reported to be worth $25m (£18m).

By most metrics, it would be hard to call either of those projects a success. The five years of the Netflix deal yielded five shows, including the six-part series Harry & Meghan and two series of the lifestyle show With Love, Meghan, drawing underwhelming streaming numbers . The deal was replaced last year by an arrangement giving Netflix a first look at any pitches from the couple. Only one new Archewell production has been announced so far this year.

title.en: Sword attack at Swedish school kills one, injures three

summary.en: A sword attack occurred at a school in Fagersta, central Sweden, resulting in one fatality and three injuries. The incident has deeply affected the small town of 13,000 residents as schools reopened.

body.en:
A man armed with a sword has attacked students at a Swedish secondary school, killing one person and injuring three, and police shot and detained him, local authorities say.

The incident occurred on Friday afternoon at the Brinell high school in the central Swedish town of Fagersta, which has about 13,000 ‌residents.

The school had just reopened after summer recess and it was the first day back for some of its students.

Police told a press conference that the suspect was an 18-year-old man whom they shot and took into custody on suspicion of murder.

Local police chief Tommy Alriksson said officers responded quickly to the school, which has 450 students ages 16 to 20.

The local health authority said two victims were teenage boys who were severely injured.

"First it was just a regular day really. But then ... I saw a guy all covered in blood, at least down his back anyway. Then I saw the police and they flooded in," one Brinell student, Nellie, told Reuters alongside her mother Agnes Strandberg after a five-hour lockdown at the school.

Another student, Abdulrahem Salmo, said he had seen a victim with a bloody stab wound in the arm.

"Then people called the police and we ⁠just all ran from there because we were afraid," he told SVT.

Several other schools and ‌public buildings in Fagersta were also initially locked down.

"Our and the school's main focus right now is to take care of our students and our employees," ‌she told reporters.

"We are working together ... to create safety and provide support to those who need it."

Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson cancelled a speech he was due to hold on Saturday, news agency TT reported.

"Our thoughts are with all those affected," he wrote in a post on social media platform X.

Sweden's King Carl XVI Gustaf said in a statement released by the royal household that he received news of the attack "with dismay and sadness".

Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson, whose coalition leads opinion polls for next month's parliamentary election, said: "All of Sweden stands together with Fagersta at this difficult time."

According to the Aftonbladet daily, police ‌were investigating a TikTok account in connection with Friday's violence that posted a picture of a sword 20 minutes before the attack.

The 25-year-old has been living a life in exile in Pakistan for the past five years, unable to return to her home in Afghanistan over fears she will be targeted for her work as a women's rights activist.

When the Taliban took power in 2021, enforcing draconian restrictions on women's rights and basic freedoms, Amani fled across the border to continue her campaigning.

"When the Taliban took away women's rights to education and work, I could not remain silent," Amani tells SBS News.

"I joined peaceful protests to defend women's rights and the right to education. That decision changed my life forever.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Over the past few years, Pakistan has beefed up deportation laws, citing national security concerns. As a result, more than two million Afghans without a valid passport or visa have been forcibly returned. Iran has similarly implemented a large-scale campaign targeting undocumented migrants, expelling more than one million Afghans.

In Pakistan, Amani says local police search for Afghans in residential areas and markets.

The crackdown has left her fearful she could be put back into the hands of her oppressor.

"We are not only worried about losing the place where we are staying," she says.

Rights groups say deported Afghans are being returned to a country with a worsening humanitarian crisis, where almost half the population is in dire need of aid. Nearly one in 10 children under five are now suffering from wasting, with acute malnutrition worsening in two-thirds of provinces, according to Save the Children.

UN officials have described Afghanistan as "a graveyard for human rights", citing the Taliban's severe human rights restrictions against women, activists, minorities, journalists and people associated with former international forces.

Amnesty Australia campaigner Zaki Haidari tells SBS News: "We have cases of people that have been deported to Afghanistan and been killed by Taliban."

"We have cases of individuals who were deported to Afghanistan and been detained and disappeared."

It remains the only country in the world in which girls over 12 and women are prohibited from secondary and higher education . The Taliban has banned beauty salons, enforced strict dress codes, removed books by women from bookshelves, banned women from parks and their voices from public spaces.

Amnesty is calling for the restrictions on women to be classified as gender apartheid and a crime against humanity.

"The Taliban has managed to introduce different laws just to completely erase a woman from Afghanistan," Haidari says.

title.en: 'Masha and the Bear': Ukraine sanctions Russian cartoon
title.zh: 《玛莎与熊》：乌克兰制裁俄罗斯动画片

summary.zh: 乌克兰已对热门俄罗斯儿童动画片《玛莎与熊》实施制裁，此举旨在将其禁用。乌克兰文化部长称该节目为宣传，而俄罗斯则表示此举暴露了基辅“丑陋的本质”。

title.en: German army helps Poland construct a defensive barrier against Russia
title.zh: 德国军队协助波兰修建针对俄罗斯的防御屏障

summary.en: Poland is constructing a defense system, known as the East Shield, along its northern and eastern borders to protect itself from Russia, with German army engineers assisting in the construction since June.
summary.zh: 波兰正在其北部和东部边境修建一个名为“东方之盾”的防御系统，以保护自己免受俄罗斯的威胁。自六月以来，德国工兵一直在协助其北约盟友进行建设。

body.en:
Poland is building a defense system along its northern and eastern borders to protect itself from Russia. Since June, German sappers have been assisting their NATO ally with the construction of the East Shield.

Poland started to construct a defensive barrier along its border with Russia and Belarus in 2024. The East Shield defense system will eventually be around 800 kilometers long, and is intended to protect this country on NATO's eastern flank against attack from the east.

When the Polish prime minister, Donald Tusk , inspected the first completed section in November 2024, he declared that the project was meant to "deter and discourage a potential aggressor" and was "truly an investment in peace."

The Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 was a profound shock to Poland's sense of security. The Tusk government has increased defense spending in 2026 to 200 billion zlotys (around 46 billion euros, or 54 billion dollars) ― almost 5% of Poland's GDP. This means that, in relative terms, Poland has the highest defense spending of all the members of NATO . The government has also bought the most advanced weapons available, particularly from the US, and is proceeding with the construction of the East Shield, a complex defense system along its eastern border.

Since June, around 40 German sappers, or combat engineers, have been helping to establish the defenses. The German army's combat engineer unit is specially trained in blocking the movement of enemy troops. The sappers are currently deployed near Budry in Masuria, close to the border with Russia. The fence marking the border is visible from where they are working, partially obscured by a row of trees on the Polish side.

The German soldiers are installing anti-tank obstacles to impede battle tanks in the event of an attack. A yellow backhoe loader lifts the spiky concrete blocks, known as Czech hedgehogs, off a truck and places them on the muddy ground.

This installation, around 200 meters back from the border, consists of three rows of these concrete blocks. A deep ditch and another line of hedgehogs run along the border itself. A Polish officer explains that mines can quickly be laid in the zone between the two lines of Czech hedgehogs.

"The German sappers have done an excellent job," the Polish general Stanislaw Czosnek said when he inspected the works on Thursday. He added that he was "very impressed" by his German colleagues' performance.

In the six weeks since their deployment, the German engineers have laid more than a kilometer of blocks.

"We stand ready to fight for democracy and freedom," stressed the German general Tito Gante, who accompanied Czosnek on the inspection. He praised the comradely atmosphere between the German and the Polish soldiers.

title.en: France issues warning over thousands of substandard condoms
title.zh: 法国就数千个不合格避孕套发出警告

summary.en: French anti-fraud and health agencies have ordered the recall of approximately 260,000 substandard condoms. Users have been advised to consider testing for sexually transmitted infections and pregnancy due to risks of bursting or perforations.
summary.zh: 法国反欺诈和卫生机构已下令召回约26万个不合格避孕套。由于存在破裂或穿孔的风险，机构建议使用者考虑进行性传播感染和怀孕检测。

body.zh: 法国反欺诈和卫生机构已发布约 26 万个安全套的召回令。他们建议用户考虑性传播感染和妊娠测试，以防破裂或穿孔的风险。 法国反欺诈和卫生机构周五发表联合声明称，他们正在召回一百万个可能有缺陷的安全套中超过四分之一。 该公司表示，大部分产品是由亚洲供应商通过主要市场在线销售的。 当局表示，在被召回的约 26 万件避孕药具中，约有 1,000 盒或 40,000 个单独的避孕套已经售出。 当局表示：“实验室分析发现了两种不合规产品，其特点是存在破裂风险，其中一种还存在穿孔。” 反欺诈机构 DGCCRF 和 DGS 卫生机构在一份联合声明中表示，这些避孕套缺乏所需的 CE 标志，该标志表明该产品符合欧洲经济区贸易区的标准。 政府机构表示：“所发现的安全套缺乏 CE 标志、第三方合格评估，并且在大多数情况下没有法语包装。” “因此，它们被认为不合规，并可能对用户的健康和安全构成严重风险（例如性传播感染和意外怀孕）。” 声明建议使用避孕套的人接受性传播感染筛查，如果有任何怀疑的理由（例如月经推迟或推迟），请进行妊娠测试。 政府表示，在线供应商已同意删除受影响的商品并寄回召回的产品。 声明列出了日本冈本工业公司生产的两个品牌的安全套，以及 Passage du Desir 的 MyLubie 和 Friday Bae 品牌。 法国通过药店向 25 岁以下的人提供免费避孕套，无需处方，以预防性传播感染和意外怀孕。 如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您就可以始终首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

title.en: Iran's president: Time to end war in 'position of strength'
title.zh: 伊朗总统：是时候在“强势地位”下结束战争了

summary.en: Iranian media report that President Masoud Pezeshkian stated it would be a good time to end the war with the US, as Iran is in a "position of strength and dignity." He further added that Tehran would never "bow to intimidation."
summary.zh: 据伊朗媒体报道，总统马苏德·佩泽什基安表示，现在是在“强势地位和尊严”下结束与美国战争的好时机。他还补充说，德黑兰绝不会“屈服于恐吓”。

body.zh: 伊朗媒体援引马苏德·佩泽什基安的话说，现在是结束与美国的战争的好时机，“因为我们处于强大和尊严的地位”。他还表示，德黑兰永远不会“屈服于恐吓”。 据官方媒体报道，伊朗总统马苏德·佩泽什基安周五表示，现在是寻求结束与美国的战争的最佳时机。 他在一次医学会议上发表上述言论之际，德黑兰官员和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普就这场冲突发出了混杂的信息。 六月达成的部分休战协议仍处于看似模棱两可的状态，周一到期，没有任何进展或续签。 德黑兰继续严格限制通过霍尔木兹海峡的航运，而美国则试图对伊朗港口实施所谓的封锁。 特朗普本周威胁要加大对伊朗的经济压力。但美国还能对这个世界上受制裁最严厉的国家之一施加多大的压力，而美国与这个国家几乎没有任何业务往来，目前还不清楚。 正如佩泽什基安似乎暗示的那样，这可能是进行和平谈判的好时机，一位伊朗军事领导人威胁说，如果美国确实试图在经济上进一步孤立伊朗，将采取“毁灭性、惩罚性和毁灭性的反应”。 据伊朗伊斯兰共和国通讯社报道，佩泽什基安表示，战争最终必须结束。 他说：“最好今天就结束这一切，因为我们拥有力量和尊严。” 佩泽什基安说：“全世界都承认我们的胜利，并强调美国违反所有规定袭击了我们的学校、医院和基础设施，受到全世界的仇恨。” 他还认为，伊朗和美国 6 月签署的 15 点谅解备忘录摇摇欲坠，这绝不意味着伊朗的失败。 他说：“他们在这一承诺中甚至找不到任何表明投降的条款。” “所有的承诺都与对方有关。” 虽然大多数人担心的是美国，但 15 项承诺中的少数确实将责任归咎于伊朗，尽管德黑兰可能会辩称，这些承诺只是同意回到战前的状况。最值得注意的例子是允许至少暂时免费通过霍尔木兹海峡进行商业运输，以及伊朗重申不会采购或发展核武器。 据报道，佩泽什基安还告诉医生群，“在任何情况下我们都不会屈服于恐吓”，如果有必要，伊朗将抵抗“直到我们最后一口气”。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普几天后主要发表有关朝鲜半岛和朝鲜领导人金正恩的言论，并简短地回应了他的...

reflection.en: The president's statement frames peace from a position of strength and dignity, refusing intimidation. This perspective challenges us to consider the biblical call to pursue peace "as far as it depends on you," which may require a posture of humility rather than asserting power. True reconciliation often asks us to set aside perceived advantages for the...
reflection.zh: 总统的声明将和平置于实力和尊严的立场，并拒绝恐吓。这促使我们思考圣经中“尽力与所有人和平相处”的呼召，这可能需要谦卑而非强调权力。真正的和解往往要求我们为与所有人和谐相处而放下自以为是的优势。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Would even an AI disaster on the scale of Hiroshima be enough to make humankind protect itself? I fear not | Timothy Garton Ash
title.zh: 蒂莫西·加顿·阿什：即使是广岛规模的人工智能灾难，也足以让人类保护自己吗？我恐怕不会

summary.en: The article expresses concern from Silicon Valley experts that Artificial Intelligence is developing at a pace exceeding humanity's capacity to control it. The author fears that even a catastrophic AI event might not prompt sufficient self-protective measures from humankind.
summary.zh: 文章表达了硅谷专家对人工智能发展速度超出人类控制能力的担忧。作者担心，即使发生一场人工智能灾难，人类可能也无法采取足够的自我保护措施。

body.en: It’s clear here in Silicon Valley that AI is advancing faster than humans’ ability to control it. That means even sober prophecies seem optimistic Here in Silicon Valley, the experts think that within the next couple of years we’ll see an extraordinary takeoff for artificial intelligence. “Welcome to the foothills of the singularity,” as a Stanford University friend greeted me. More prosaically, the imminent breakthrough is described as “recursive self-improvement” – the point at which AI itself trains each successive model of AI, resulting in an exponential development to something which, in many significant respects, is more intelligent than us humans. As Robert Wright puts it in his book The God Test : “Never before has the near-term future … held such a wide array of not-implausible paths for humankind that would be so wildly transformative.” But will this be heaven or hell? Heaven, says Elon Musk, who predicts “an age of amazing abundance” – although he also sees a 10-20% chance of killer robots murdering us all. Hell is more likely according to Geoffrey Hinton , one of the intellectual founding fathers of AI. “My intuition is, we’re toast,” he told an interviewer in 2023. And talking to Sebastian Mallaby , author of The Infinity Machine, a book about the quest for superintelligence, Hinton estimates p(doom) – the probability of human extinction – at 50%, “because I haven’t got a clue how to estimate the real number”. “As soon as evolution [of AI] kicks in, we’re fucked,” he adds cheerfully. But whether it’s God or Godzilla, artificial superintelligence is just around the corner. Timothy Garton Ash is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...
body.zh: 在硅谷，人工智能的发展速度明显快于人类控制它的能力。这意味着即使是清醒的预言也显得乐观。在硅谷，专家们认为，在未来几年内，我们将看到人工智能的非凡腾飞。 “欢迎来到奇点的山麓，”一位斯坦福大学的朋友向我打招呼。更通俗地说，即将到来的突破被描述为“递归自我改进”——人工智能本身训练每个连续的人工智能模型，从而实现指数级发展，在许多重要方面比我们人类更聪明。正如罗伯特·赖特（Robert Wright）在他的《上帝的考验》一书中所说：“在不久的将来……从来没有为人类提供过如此广泛的并非难以置信的道路，并且具有如此巨大的变革性。”但这到底是天堂还是地狱呢？埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 表示，这是天堂，他预测“一个令人惊叹的丰富时代”，尽管他也认为杀手机器人有 10-20% 的可能性谋杀我们所有人。人工智能创始人之一杰弗里·辛顿 (Geoffrey Hinton) 认为，地狱更有可能发生。 “我的直觉是，我们完蛋了，”他在 2023 年对一位采访者说道。在与《无限机器》（一本关于探索超级智能的书）的作者 Sebastian Mallaby 交谈时，Hinton 估计 p(doom)——人类灭绝的概率——为 50%，“因为我不知道如何估计真实的数字”。 “一旦[人工智能]进化开始，我们就完蛋了，”他高兴地补充道。但无论是上帝还是哥斯拉，人工智能都指日可待。蒂莫西·加顿·阿什 (Timothy Garton Ash) 是《卫报》专栏作家继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of AI, as highlighted in this report, presents a profound challenge to human foresight and prudence. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us that the wise foresee danger and take refuge, while the naive press on and suffer the consequences. As we navigate these complex technological frontiers, may we seek the wisdom to discern potential harms and...
reflection.zh: 正如这篇报道所强调的，人工智能的迅速发展对人类的远见和审慎提出了严峻挑战。箴言27:12提醒我们，通达人预见危险就藏躲，愚蒙人却往前行，自受亏损。在我们探索这些复杂的技术前沿时，愿我们寻求智慧，辨明潜在的危害，并负责任地行动，以保护我们共同的未来。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: ‘She’s not afraid of anyone’: the prison writings of one of Hong Kong’s last outspoken democracy activists
title.zh: “她无所畏惧”：香港最后一位直言不讳的民主活动家的狱中手稿

summary.en: Chow Hang-tung, a prominent Hong Kong democracy activist, has been detained since 2021 and continues to write from prison on various subjects, including freedom and the Tiananmen Square vigil.
summary.zh: 香港著名民主活动家邹幸彤自2021年被拘留以来，一直在狱中撰写关于自由和天安门广场守夜等各种主题的文章。

body.en: Chow Hang-tung has been detained since 2021, and written about everything from clothes to Tiananmen Square and the meaning of freedom Tiananmen Square vigil organisers in Hong Kong found guilty of ‘inciting subversion’ In one essay written from prison, Chow Hang-tung worries about her hairstyle before court appearances because there are no combs or mirrors in her cell. “In a place like prison, where anything that is personal is stripped away, it’s even more important to hold on to every means by which you can express yourself,” she writes. “Don’t let uniform, depersonalised rules, dress codes, schedules, and behavioural requirements grind down your edges and mould you into a ‘model citizen’”. Continue reading...
body.zh: 周恒东自 2021 年以来一直被拘留，并撰写了从服装到天安门广场以及自由的意义等各种内容。香港天安门广场守夜活动组织者被判犯有“煽动颠覆罪”。在一篇在狱中写的文章中，周恒东对自己出庭前的发型感到担忧，因为她的牢房里没有梳子或镜子。 “在监狱这样的地方，任何个人的东西都被剥夺了，更重要的是要坚持一切可以表达自己的方式，”她写道。 “不要让统一的、非个性化的规则、着装规范、时间表和行为要求磨掉你的棱角，把你塑造成‘模范公民’”。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In the face of human authority, there are moments when conscience compels individuals to prioritize a higher calling. Chow Hang-tung's continued outspokenness from prison, despite her detention, reflects a deep conviction that some truths must be spoken, regardless of the cost. This echoes the biblical principle of obeying Yahweh rather than human beings...
reflection.zh: 面对人类的权威，有时良知会驱使个人优先遵循更高的呼召。邹幸彤尽管身陷囹圄，却仍在狱中持续发声，这反映出一种深刻的信念，即有些真理无论代价如何都必须被说出来。这与圣经中当人的命令与雅伟的原则相冲突时，我们必须顺从雅伟而非人的教导不谋而合。

verse.textEn: We must obey God rather than human beings!
verse.textZh: 顺从神，不顺从人，是应当的。

title.en: Tesla recalls nearly 3m vehicles in China over door handle safety risks
title.zh: 特斯拉在中国召回近300万辆汽车，涉及车门把手安全风险

summary.en: Tesla and other carmakers are recalling over 4 million vehicles in China, including nearly 3 million Teslas, due to safety concerns primarily related to hidden door handles. This action follows an announcement by Chinese authorities to ban such door handle designs.
summary.zh: 特斯拉及其他汽车制造商正在中国召回超过400万辆汽车，其中包括近300万辆特斯拉，主要原因是与隐藏式车门把手相关的安全隐患。此举是在中国当局宣布将禁止此类车门把手设计之后进行的。

body.en: Recall comes after Chinese authorities said it would ban hidden car door handles commonly seen on Tesla models Tesla and other carmakers are making a major recall of more than 4m vehicles in China over safety concerns mostly related to their door handles, according to Chinese authorities on Friday. The US carmaker is recalling about 2.98m China-made and imported EVs including Model 3, Model Y, Model X and Model S over door-handle safety risks, according to China’s state administration for market regulation. Continue reading...
body.zh: 据中国当局周五称，中国当局表示将禁止特斯拉车型上常见的隐藏式车门把手，特斯拉和其他汽车制造商正在中国大规模召回超过 400 万辆汽车，原因主要是与车门把手有关的安全问题。据中国国家市场监管总局称，由于门把手安全风险，这家美国汽车制造商正在召回约 298 万辆中国制造和进口电动汽车，包括 Model 3、Model Y、Model X 和 Model S。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This recall highlights the importance of foresight and precaution in design and manufacturing. While innovation is valued, true wisdom involves anticipating potential dangers and taking necessary steps to ensure public safety, rather than waiting for penalties.
reflection.zh: 此次召回凸显了设计和制造中预见性和预防措施的重要性。虽然创新值得称赞，但真正的智慧在于预见潜在危险并采取必要措施确保公共安全，而不是等到付出代价。

title.en: These bookshops let Chinese readers question their country - now the doors are closing
title.zh: 这些书店曾让中国读者质疑他们的国家——现在它们正在关闭

summary.en: Independent bookstores in Hong Kong, which offered mainland Chinese readers a glimpse into a different, freer world, are now facing closure.
summary.zh: 香港的独立书店曾为中国大陆读者提供了一个了解不同、更自由世界的窗口，但现在这些书店正面临关闭。

body.en:
When Chen Zhu heads to Hong Kong from mainland China every month, there's one place she always goes: Hunter Bookstore.

Founded four years ago by a former councillor, the independent bookshop has earned a reputation for stocking what authorities would consider sensitive books - accounts of Hong Kong's pro-democracy campaigners to famous allegories on authoritarianism, such as George Orwell's Animal Farm or Hajime Isayama's Manga series Attack on Titan.

It's a short journey from Zhu's home in Guangzhou on China's southern coast to the crowded street in Hong Kong's Sham Shui Po district, where Hunter is sandwiched between fabric sellers, garages and trendy cafes.

But, for the 23-year-old, it is also a passage into a different, freer world - where she can find answers to forbidden questions.

When she learned the bookshop had been raided by police in late June, Zhu broke into tears: "I was devastated."

Hong Kong saw a boom in independent bookshops after huge pro-democracy protests rocked the city in 2019. But it has been increasingly difficult for them to survive as China's control over the city has grown.

While Beijing defends its far-reaching National Security Law (NSL) as essential for stability, many Hong Kongers and rights groups argue it has crushed free speech. Thousands of locals, including activists and former lawmakers, have left in recent years, as tough new security laws have led to a slew of arrests and convictions.

When police searched Hunter Bookstore on 24 June, they accused owner Letitia Wong, 33, and a 32-year-old man, of violating those laws and arrested them for sedition and money laundering. They deny the charges and have since been released on bail.

In March, they arrested the owner of Book Punch, along with three employees on the same charges, and reportedly seized copies of a biography on Jimmy Lai, the jailed democracy campaigner.

On 15 July, when the annual Hong Kong Book Fair opened, national security police searched two more independent bookshops, Greenfield Bookstore and Have a Nice Stay, arresting five people for sedition. They, too, have been released on bail.

At the end of the month Greenfield posted on social media, saying: "Our store will be closing after our lease expires. Thank you for walking with us, through wind and rain, for 50 years since our opening." It was the third independent bookshop to shut within a month.

These bookshops have long had a loyal following not just in Hong Kong, but also among many mainland Chinese readers. Some like Zhu travel to the city in search of a single book.

For 19-year-old Li from Shanghai, who didn't give her first name, these are places where she "can see so many possibilities, and where existing ideas can be challenged". Others treasure them as spaces that offer a...
body.zh: 陈竹每个月从大陆去香港时，都会去一个地方：亨特书店。 这家独立书店由一名前议员于四年前创立，因出售当局认为敏感的书籍而闻名——从香港民主运动人士的记述到有关威权主义的著名寓言，例如乔治·奥威尔的《动物农场》或谏山创的漫画系列《进击的巨人》。 从朱在中国南部沿海广州的家到香港深水埗区拥挤的街道只有很短的路程，亨特夹在布料摊贩、车库和时尚咖啡馆之间。 但是，对于这位 23 岁的女孩来说，这也是通往一个不同的、更自由的世界的通道——在那里她可以找到禁忌问题的答案。 当得知六月下旬书店被警方突击搜查时，朱女士泪流满面：“我崩溃了。” 2019 年大规模民主抗议活动震撼香港后，香港独立书店蓬勃发展。但随着中国对香港的控制不断加强，独立书店的生存变得越来越困难。 尽管北京捍卫其影响深远的国家安全法对于稳定至关重要，但许多香港人和人权组织认为该法压制了言论自由。近年来，由于严厉的新安全法导致大量逮捕和定罪，包括活动人士和前立法者在内的数千名当地人离开了。 6 月 24 日，警方搜查 Hunter 书店时，指控 33 岁的店主 Letitia Wong 和一名 32 岁的男子违反了这些法律，并以煽动叛乱和洗钱罪逮捕了他们。他们否认这些指控，并已获得保释。 今年三月，他们以同样的罪名逮捕了 Book Punch 的老板和三名员工，据报道，他们还查获了一本关于被监禁的民主运动人士黎智英 (Jimmy Lai) 的传记。 7月15日，一年一度的香港书展开幕，国安警察搜查了另外两家独立书店——绿田书店和Have a Nice Stay，并以煽动罪逮捕了五人。他们也已被保释。 月底，格林菲尔德在社交媒体上发文称：“我们的店将在租约到期后关闭。感谢您与我们一起走过开业50年的风雨。”这是一个月内第三家关闭的独立书店。 这些书店长期以来不仅在香港而且在许多中国大陆读者中拥有忠实的追随者。有些人像朱一样前往城市寻找一本书。 对于来自上海的 19 岁李（未透露姓名）来说，这些地方是她“可以看到如此多的可能性，并且可以挑战现有想法的地方”。其他人则珍视它们，认为它们是提供...的空间。

reflection.en: The closure of these independent bookstores in Hong Kong highlights a deep human longing for truth and the freedom it brings. Yahweh's word reminds us that knowing the truth is intrinsically linked to liberation, offering a path to understanding beyond narrow confines. Even when access to diverse perspectives is restricted, the spirit of inquiry and the...
reflection.zh: 香港这些独立书店的关闭，凸显了人类对真理及其所带来自由的深切渴望。雅伟的话语提醒我们，认识真理与获得自由紧密相连，它提供了一条超越狭隘限制的理解之路。即使获取多元视角的途径受限，求知和追求真理的精神依然强大。

verse.textEn: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.
verse.textZh: 你们必晓得真理，真理必叫你们得以自由。

title.en: Tiananmen Square vigil organisers in Hong Kong found guilty of ‘inciting subversion’
title.zh: 天安门守夜活动组织者在香港被判“煽动颠覆”罪名成立

summary.en: Two leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance, Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung, were found guilty of "incitement to subversion" under a 2020 national security law. They were prosecuted for organizing annual vigils commemorating China’s 1989 Tiananmen crackdown.
summary.zh: 香港支联会领袖李卓人及邹幸彤根据2020年国家安全法，被裁定“煽动颠覆国家政权罪”成立。他们因组织纪念1989年中国天安门镇压的年度烛光晚会而受到起诉。

body.en: UK Foreign Office condemns use of national security law to convict activists Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung Two Hong Kong activists who organised annual vigils marking China’s deadly Tiananmen crackdown in 1989 have been found guilty of “incitement to subversion” in one of the most high-profile cases in Hong Kong since Beijing imposed its national security law in 2020. Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, “incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power”, a press summary handed out to reporters said. The defendants each face a maximum penalty of 10 years in jail, with sentencing expected at a later date. Continue reading...
body.zh: 香港联盟领导人李卓人和周恒东根据 2020 年国家安全法接受审判 两名香港活动人士组织了年度守夜活动，纪念中国 1989 年致命的天安门镇压，被判犯有“煽动颠覆罪”，这是自北京于 2020 年实施国家安全法以来香港最引人注目的案件之一。李卓人，69 岁，周恒东，一份发给记者的新闻摘要称，41号“煽动他人以非法手段组织、策划、实施或者参与颠覆国家政权的行为”。继续阅读...

title.en: Hong Kong's Tiananmen activists guilty in national security trial
title.zh: 香港天安门活动人士在国家安全审判中被判有罪

summary.en: Three activists in Hong Kong have been found guilty of inciting others to subvert state power under a national security law introduced by China.
summary.zh: 香港三名活动人士根据中国实施的国家安全法，被判煽动他人颠覆国家政权罪名成立。

body.en:
Two Hong Kong activists who organised annual vigils to commemorate the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown have been found guilty of inciting others to subvert state power under the city's controversial national security law.

Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, face a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison after being convicted under the China-introduced law. Sentencing is expected at a later date.

Lee and Chow "incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power", according to a summary on Friday. Chow told the court in May the law itself was on trial.

Hong Kong used to be one of the only places in Chinese territory where people could gather to mark the deadly 1989 crackdown against pro-democracy protesters.

Authorities banned these gatherings in 2020, citing Covid-19 policies, but they have never resumed. This was also the year the national security law, which makes illegal a wider range of dissenting acts, officially came into force.

In mainland China, authorities have banned even oblique references to the 1989 crackdown.

In the courtroom, Chow smiled as the verdict was read out, while Lee showed little emotion as he made a heart gesture and folded his hands to show his gratitude to those in the gallery.

Lee, a lawmaker, and Chow, a lawyer, were also leaders of the now-defunct Hong Kong Alliance (HKA), which has been described as a "toxic tumour" by Chinese authorities.

The HKA was founded in May 1989 to support students holding pro-democracy rallies. Weeks later, the Communist Party crushed pro-democracy protests in Beijing's Tiananmen Square with troops and tanks. Estimates of the death toll range from a few hundred to many thousands.

Over the next three decades, HKA called on authorities to accept responsibility for the crackdown, free dissidents and introduce democratic reform.

Rights group Amnesty International has said the case "relies on vague, overly broad and arbitrary definitions of 'subversion'".

Sarah Brooks, Amnesty International's deputy regional director, said Chow and Lee had "not committed any recognisable crime".

"Chow Hang-tung and Lee Cheuk-yan are prisoners of conscience who should never have been prosecuted in the first place. They must be released immediately and unconditionally," she added.

Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch, said the convictions showed "how public displays of mourning have become a crime in Hong Kong".

In a separate case, Chow was arrested in June 2021 for "inciting" the public to take part in that year's vigil and later found guilty.

However, Hong Kong's top court overturned that conviction in 2022 , with a judge ruling the police hadn't properly justified the vigil's ban.

body.zh: 根据香港备受争议的国家安全法，两名组织年度守夜活动纪念 1989 年天安门广场镇压活动的香港活动人士被判犯有煽动他人颠覆国家政权罪。 根据中国出台的法律，69岁的李卓人和41岁的周恒东被定罪后，最高可判处10年监禁。预计将在晚些时候宣判。 根据周五的摘要，李和周“煽动他人以非法手段组织、策划、实施或者参与行为，以颠覆国家政权”。周五月份告诉法庭，该法律本身正在接受审判。 香港曾经是中国境内唯一一个人们可以聚集纪念1989年镇压亲民主抗议者的地方。 当局以 Covid-19 政策为由，在 2020 年禁止了这些聚会，但从未恢复。今年也是《国家安全法》正式生效的一年，该法将范围更广的异议行为定为非法。 在中国大陆，当局甚至禁止间接提及 1989 年的镇压行动。 在法庭上，周先生在宣读判决时微笑着，而李则没有任何情绪，他做了一个心形手势并双手合十，向旁听席上的人们表示感谢。 立法会议员李和律师周先生也是现已解散的香港联谊会（HKA）的领导人，该联谊会被中国当局称为“毒瘤”。 香港学生会成立于1989年5月，旨在支持学生举行民主集会。几周后，共产党用军队和坦克镇压了北京天安门广场的民主抗议活动。死亡人数估计从数百人到数千人不等。 在接下来的三十年里，香港协会呼吁当局承担镇压责任，释放异见人士并推行民主改革。 人权组织国际特赦组织表示，此案“依赖于‘颠覆’的模糊、过于宽泛和武断的定义”。 国际特赦组织区域副主任莎拉·布鲁克斯 (Sarah Brooks) 表示，周和李“没有犯下任何可识别的罪行”。 她补充说：“周恒东和李卓人是良心犯，他们本来就不应该受到起诉。他们必须立即无条件释放。” 人权观察组织亚洲部主任伊莱恩·皮尔森(Elaine Pearson)表示，这些定罪表明“在香港公开表达哀悼已成为犯罪行为”。 在另一起案件中，周先生于 2021 年 6 月因“煽动”公众参加当年的守夜活动而被捕，后来被判有罪。 然而，香港最高法院于 2022 年推翻了这一判决，法官裁定警方没有适当证明禁止守夜活动的合理性。 周恒东...

title.en: Hong Kong convicts Tiananmen vigil leaders
title.zh: 香港裁定天安门守夜活动领导人有罪

summary.en: Two pro-democracy activists in Hong Kong have been found guilty of inciting subversion, a verdict that has drawn widespread criticism for signaling a decline in freedom of expression in the city.
summary.zh: 两名香港民主运动人士被判煽动颠覆罪名成立，这一判决因预示着该市言论自由的恶化而受到广泛批评。

body.en:
The two pro-democracy Tiananmen activists were found guilty of inciting subversion. The high-profile case has been widely criticized for highlighting the deterioration of freedom of expression.

A Hong Kong court on Thursday convicted two pro-democracy Tiananmen activists under Beijing's  controversial national security law for "incitement to subversion."

Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, had organized candlelight vigils to mark Beijing's deadly 1989 Tiananmen crackdown. They were charged in 2021 and both pleaded not guilty.

They face a maximum prison term of 10 years and are expected to be sentenced at a later date.

Germany and France on Friday morning  published a joint statement to say that both "deeply regret the guilty verdict against human ​rights lawyer and democracy activist Chow Hang-tung."

The statement called for the immediate release of Chow and added that "peaceful advocacy for human rights does not constitute a crime."

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council, which oversees the island's China policy, expressed "deep regret and sorrow" and called on the Chinese Communist Party and Hong Kong government to "immediately release those detained in this case." 

Hong Kong judicial officials claimed the pair "incited other persons to organize, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power."

Prosecutors had argued they "endanger(ed) national security in the name of human rights."

Public commemorations of the deadly Tiananmen crackdown , when Beijing sent troops and tanks to crush protests calling for political reform in and around the capital's Tiananmen Square, have been effectively banned since the 2020 imposition of the national security law on Hong Kong.

The controversial law came after Hong Kong's massive anti-government, pro-democracy protests in 2019.

title.en: After two decades, China is preparing its boldest Moon mission yet
title.zh: 中国正准备执行二十年来最雄心勃勃的探月任务

summary.en: China is preparing its most ambitious moon mission in two decades, scheduled for next month. The mission aims to explore the lunar surface, specifically searching for water.
summary.zh: 中国正准备在下个月执行其二十年来最雄心勃勃的探月任务。此次任务旨在探索月球表面，特别是寻找水资源。

body.en:
How do you explore a place where the sun never shines? China's space program will soon embark on one of the most innovative lunar exploration missions in recent years.

We’ve known for nearly two decades that some form of water exists on the moon. What we still don’t know is exactly how much accessible water ice lies inside permanently shadowed craters, how deeply it is buried or what form it takes.

What we do know is that accessing that water ice will be a real challenge: it is found at the bottom of deep, hard-to-traverse craters where the sun never shines, remaining untouched for billions of years at temperatures well below –200C. These are among the most valuable places on the moon, but the hardest to reach and explore.

Lunar exploration has come a long way since the Soviet Union’s Luna-1 probe reached the moon's vicinity in January 1959. The Apollo missions and their successors showed the challenge is no longer simply to reach the moon. It is to explore places human and conventional rovers cannot easily go, and ultimately determine whether the moon itself can provide some of the resources that future explorers will need.

China has spent two decades building an increasingly ambitious lunar exploration program, named after Chang'e, the ancient Chinese goddess of the moon. The Chang'e-7 mission is expected to set course for our celestial neighbour later this month, although a recent failure involving a different Chinese rocket has introduced some uncertainty over the launch date. Here’s what makes this latest mission so interesting.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The mission will test several novel approaches to lunar exploration. It will consist of an orbiter, a lander, a rover and a hopper.

In addition, the Queqiao-2 lunar relay satellite is already in place. Launched separately in March 2024, it subsequently supported the Chang'e-6 mission and will facilitate communication between Earth and the lunar surface during the Chang'e-7 mission.

We don’t know precisely where the mission will land, but a site on or near an illuminated ridge close to the Shackleton crater in the Lunar South Pole’s Aitken region is a prime candidate.

The hopper will be the mission’s real star. Unlike a wheeled rover, it’s designed to leap over broken terrain and descend into craters where sunlight never reaches, places conventional vehicles may simply be unable to enter.

Adding it to the mission makes sense, given the steep crater walls, broken terrain, permanent shadow and the need for autonomous navigation and communications.

title.en: Indonesia-China naval drill raises neutrality concerns
title.zh: 印尼与中国海军演习引发中立担忧

summary.en: Indonesia's participation in a limited naval exercise with China near Taiwan has raised questions about its long-standing nonaligned foreign policy.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚与中国海军在台湾附近举行了有限的海上演习，这引发了对其长期不结盟外交政策的担忧。

body.en:
Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill.

Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. 

An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy.  

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  

Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022.

Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training."

Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance.

"It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said.

However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan .

"Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said.

body.zh: 印度尼西亚维持不结盟的外交政策，但雅加达有限地参与与中国海军在台湾附近举行的低级别海军演习，引起了密切关注。 8月12日，一艘印度尼西亚护卫舰短暂参加了与中国人民解放军海军在台湾东海岸附近海域举行的海军演习，台北向雅加达询问其参加演习的原因。 印度尼西亚海军护卫舰 KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai 与中国海军导弹护卫舰红河号一起进行了雅加达所说的“穿越演习”。这次演习是在台湾一年一度的汉光军演期间进行的。 印度尼西亚外交部发言人表示，他们完全意识到演习地点“使其特别敏感”，但强调其船只的存在“只是其返回印度尼西亚的过境路线的一部分”。据《台北时报》报道，这艘印尼舰艇在与俄罗斯海军演习后正从俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克返回。 中国8月11日宣布演习后，台湾陆委会谴责北京的“挑衅”。台北还要求外交部“提供更多细节”。 北京认为台湾是中国领土，并誓言要让这个自治岛屿与大陆“统一”，必要时会使用武力。特别是自美国前众议院议长南希·佩洛西 2022 年访问台北以来，解放军在台湾频繁进行军事演习，加大了对台湾的压力。 在台北和华盛顿的反应中，印度尼西亚海军表示，其与中国海军的活动“本质上不是战斗活动”，并且“无意进行战斗训练”。 台湾淡江大学国际事务与战略研究所副教授林英宇告诉德国之声，中国与印尼的演习没有什么战术意义。 他说：“这不像联合海上演习那么实际，但中国希望宣示其在该海域的能力。” 不过，日本国际问题研究所研究台印尼关系的客座研究员拉蒂·卡比纳瓦(Ratih Kabinawa)告诉德国之声，无论演习的意义如何，印尼都应该预料到台湾会做出一些反应。 “无论你喜欢与否，印度尼西亚现在都被拖入了这种地缘政治游戏，”她说。 卡比纳瓦补充说，此次演习是中国迄今为止用来证明其恐吓台湾合理性的最低级别的海军活动之一。 她说：“印度尼西亚在这方面也必须保持谨慎。”她补充说，雅加达应该“不要太天真”，认为参加与中国的“定期演习”不会引起人们的担忧……

reflection.en: In a world of complex geopolitical dynamics, nations often strive to maintain peace and neutrality. Indonesia's efforts to navigate its foreign policy amidst regional tensions reflect the ongoing challenge of living at peace with all, as far as it depends on them. This pursuit requires wisdom and a steadfast commitment to de-escalation and understanding.

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

Personal injury specialist Slater and Gordon has been engaged by one of now three women allegedly hired as adult entertainers to party with five Swans players at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne on Monday morning.

The firm has been asked to determine whether the woman "involved in the alleged sexual assaults" has grounds to file a civil claim, says senior lawyer Jackson Pannam.

''Everyone deserves to be safe going about their life, at home, at work and in public spaces without risk of being assaulted or harmed,'' he said in a statement on Saturday.

According to Mr Pannam, the woman, who contacted police immediately after the alleged assault, has had her world turned upside down and is navigating an "incredibly traumatic experience".

The sanctions on the five men are separate to the police investigations into sexual assault allegations and the events at East Melbourne's Pullman Hotel in the early hours of Monday morning.

Victoria Police and Sydney released separate statements on Saturday, with the Swans repeating a previous statement that no club representatives other than the five suspended players were in the hotel room in question.

"The Sydney Swans supports the action taken by Victoria Police in releasing today's statement regarding the investigation," the Swans said in their statement.

"The Sydney Swans categorically confirms that no member of staff is involved in the investigation. This includes being in the hotel room central to the police investigation.

Victoria Police said their investigation was ongoing and no charges have been laid.

title.en: Can Australia rebuild social cohesion? Inquiry hears calls for change
title.zh: 澳大利亚能否重建社会凝聚力？调查听取改革呼吁

summary.en: A Royal Commission in Australia is examining how to combat antisemitism and rebuild social cohesion, specifically addressing the challenge of doing so without suppressing legitimate debate.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚皇家委员会正在审视如何在不压制辩论的情况下打击反犹主义并重建社会凝聚力。

body.en:
Experts, advocates and community leaders are calling for stronger social cohesion and action on antisemitism, telling an inquiry "we need to break the cycle".

Over four days of hearings this week, commissioner Virginia Bell heard concerns about declining satisfaction with democracy, social media polarisation, racism, self-censorship and the breakdown of relationships between religious and cultural communities.

The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion also heard proposals for stronger education about Jewish Australians, better recognition of migrants’ qualifications and more effective approaches to tackling prejudice.

But the hearings also exposed difficult questions about what social cohesion should mean, including how Australia can combat discrimination without silencing debate.

The royal commission, launched in response to the December 2025 Bondi terror attack, is in its ninth and final block of hearings, with its final report due in December.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Professors Nicholas Biddle and Matthew Gray, both from the Australian National University, fronted the royal commission on Monday, speaking to reporters about democratic attitudes in Australia and responses about declining satisfaction with democracy.

Their June report found that satisfaction with democracy fell to its lowest level since January 2023, while principled support for democracy increased. Professor Gray said multiple factors could be at play, including social media undermining support for democracy.

"We conclude that efforts to counter antisemitism will be limited unless they also address the platforms through which distrust, polarisation and extremist narratives circulate," Gray told the commission.

He argued targeted interventions, particularly for young Australians with low educational attainment and low levels of principled democratic support, would be more effective than universal attempts to counter antisemitism.

"Because trust in core institutions is closely associated with democratic commitment, consideration should be given to how government agencies, education systems and public communications practices could be made more transparent, accountable and credible, particularly in communities experiencing disadvantage," Gray said.

Ahmed Hegazi, a strategic adviser, and his friend Joel Lazar, the chief executive of the Jewish Climate Network, also expressed concern about polarisation and emphasised the importance of cross-cultural communication.

"Humans who know their neighbours don't feel they are threats and they don't fear them, they feel connected to them," Hegazi said. "We need to break the cycle."

title.en: ACT signs on to federal firearms buyback scheme
title.zh: 首都领地签署联邦枪支回购计划

summary.en: The Australian Capital Territory has joined New South Wales in adopting the federal government's gun buyback scheme, which was established after a mass shooting occurred in Bondi in December.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚首都领地已加入新南威尔士州的行列，参与联邦政府的枪支回购计划。该计划是在去年12月邦迪发生大规模枪击事件后设立的。

body.en:
The ACT has become the latest jurisdiction to sign on to a federal gun buyback scheme.

The territory has reached an agreement with the federal government for the scheme to remove firearms, which was set up following the Bondi mass shooting in December.

It is just the second jurisdiction to join the scheme after NSW announced on Sunday it would be part of the buyback.

It's estimated 14 per cent of the ACT's 7000 firearms licence holders will be affected by a proposed cap on guns.

Under the scheme, 75 per cent of the cost of compensation to firearm holders, administration and gun destruction will be paid for by the federal government.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the government would work closely with the ACT to keep more guns off the streets.

"We're taking action to strengthen Australia's gun laws and keep our communities safe," he said in a statement.

"National gun reform is an important part of making sure an anti-Semitic terrorist attack like we saw at Bondi can't happen again."

ACT Chief Minister Andrew Barr said while the majority of gun owners were responsible, further safety measures were needed.

"The buyback scheme will provide compensation while helping deliver further community safety outcomes," he said.

"The ACT has some of the strongest firearms laws in the country, and this agreement supports our ongoing efforts to further reduce the risk of firearms falling into the wrong hands."

National cabinet agreed to strengthen firearm restrictions across Australia following the Bondi attack, where 15 people died after two gunmen opened fire at a Hanukkah festival.

But the scheme faces opposition from some jurisdictions, with conservative governments in the Northern Territory, Tasmania and Queensland declining to sign up.

Western Australia had already operated its own gun buyback and does not have plans to be part of a second one linked to the federal government.

title.en: The missing piece of evidence Australia is still pursuing after Zomi Frankcom's killing
title.zh: 佐米·弗兰克科姆遇害案：澳大利亚仍在追究缺失的证据

body.en:
The family of slain Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom say they will continue their fight for justice, with missing drone audio remaining one of the central unanswered questions about her death.

Israel this week announced it would not prosecute those responsible for the killing of Frankcom and six of her World Central Kitchen colleagues in Gaza in April 2024, despite conceding "serious failures" that led to the mistaken-identity drone strikes by the Israel Defense Force (IDF) .

On Thursday, Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the decision was an "outrage" , and she had no confidence in the IDF's Military Advocate General's two-year investigation "given the many unanswered questions".

Among the unresolved issues is a missing piece of drone footage audio, which Israel refused to hand over to Australia's independent inquiry, headed by retired Air Chief Marshal Mark Binskin, despite requests by the federal government.

According to his report — which found the killing was due to mistaken identity and procedural failings but not a deliberate targeting of aid workers — Binskin was given access to 90 minutes of unedited drone footage, but it did not include an audio track.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese renewed calls for the audio to be released in parliamentary Question Time on Thursday, saying it's part of the transparency Australia has called for "from day one".

Israeli ambassador to Australia Hillel Newman on Friday told ABC radio the audio may contain "intelligence information" and there was nothing in it to cast doubt on the findings which cleared the IDF of criminal misconduct.

In a statement on Thursday, Frankcom's family called on the government to continue pressing Israel to release the audio and to "pursue all available legal avenues for an independent and credible investigation to be conducted".

However Dr Emily Crawford, an international law professor at the University of Sydney, said Australia's options were limited.

"In all states, the scope to argue that national security grounds required for information not to be released, they're fairly paramount," she told SBS News.

"We've seen that the Netanyahu government is reluctant to assist in these kinds of things, so I can't imagine there's really going to be any movement on that."

The missing audio is just one of the unanswered questions surrounding the strike, with Wong saying the IDF had failed to explain how two strikes occurred after the initial strike, in breach of the IDF's rules of engagement.

title.en: What Europe's shrinking rivers reveal, and why Australia should take notice
title.zh: 欧洲河流萎缩揭示了什么，以及澳大利亚为何应引起关注

summary.en: Discoveries from Europe's shrinking rivers highlight environmental challenges that extend globally, prompting other regions like Australia to observe and learn.
summary.zh: 欧洲河流萎缩所揭示的发现，指出了远远超出该大陆的挑战。

body.en:
In northern Bulgaria, water in the Danube River has fallen so low that scientists say an ancient mammal has once again been exposed to the world.

The remains of what is believed to be a woolly mammoth were uncovered in late July and hailed by historians as a "very important" discovery.

Near the Serbian village of Prahovo, the rusted vessels and broken masts of German warships also resurfaced from the riverbank this month.

"This has literally never happened before; these wrecks ... have never been visible like this. They've always been completely submerged; what we're seeing now is utterly unprecedented," he said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The discoveries along Europe's second-longest river come as parts of central and eastern Europe experience prolonged summer heatwaves and drought conditions.

Armin Fojskic, a member of the Zenica Fishermen Association, said if conditions don't ease, he expects a large number of fish to die in European rivers.

"Low levels of water are critical for the fish, especially if it is extremely low, and these past days it has really been extremely low," Fojskic said.

"The main danger for fish is oxygenation of the river; when water flow drops, the river loses oxygen and fish start to suffocate."

According to the European Drought Observatory, about half of Europe and the United Kingdom experienced drought at various levels of intensity in July. Major wildfires have also burned across the continent .

But Peter Gleick, a hydro-climatologist and co-founder of the Pacific Institute in California, believes what Europe has experienced is not in line with normal weather fluctuations.

"Weather is always variable. We always have droughts. We always have floods somewhere at some time ... but what we're seeing now is extreme events worsened by human-caused climate change," Gleick told SBS News.

"We're dumping greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. We know that's warming the planet. We know that it's altering these extreme events by making them more extreme, more frequent, and more intense."

Gleick said the extreme patterns affecting rivers in Europe are similarly impacting water systems across the globe.

"In the western United States, the Colorado River, which is ... shared by seven [US] states and Mexico, is at record low levels," he said.

reflection.en: The shrinking rivers in Europe, and their global implications, remind us of our ancient call to care for the earth. Yahweh placed humanity in creation not just to enjoy it, but to actively work and tend to it. This news invites us to reflect on our stewardship and responsibility towards the natural world.
reflection.zh: 欧洲河流的萎缩及其全球影响，提醒我们人类古老的使命，即看顾大地。雅伟将人类安置在受造界中，不仅是为了享受，更是要积极地耕耘和看守。这则新闻邀请我们反思对自然世界的管家职责和责任。
